14: # TSDoc, Typed Error Classes & Async Patterns
15: 
16: TSDoc, typed-error, and asynchronous programming patterns for TypeScript files.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines TypeScript documentation, typed-error, and async implementation patterns.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - Documenting TypeScript APIs with TSDoc
29: - Defining or handling typed errors
30: - Implementing concurrent or failure-tolerant async operations
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. TSDOC DOCUMENTATION
35: 
36: ### TSDoc Format
37: 
38: TypeScript uses TSDoc format. Unlike JSDoc, TSDoc does not include `{type}` annotations because TypeScript has native types.
39: 
40: ### Function Documentation
41: 
42: ```typescript
43: /**
44:  * Look up trigger-index entries matching a query.
45:  *
46:  * Scans the generated trigger index for phrase matches, then ranks the
47:  * surviving packets by how many distinct phrases each one matched.
48:  *
49:  * @param query - Search query text
50:  * @param options - Lookup configuration
51:  * @returns Array of matching trigger entries sorted by relevance
52:  * @throws {@link SpecFolderError} If the spec folder cannot be resolved
53:  * @throws {@link ValidationError} If query exceeds maximum length
54:  *
55:  * @example
56:  * ```typescript
57:  * const results = await lookupTriggers('authentication', {
58:  *   limit: 5,
59:  *   specFolder: 'specs/007-auth',
60:  * });
61:  * ```
62:  */
63: export async function lookupTriggers(
64:   query: string,
65:   options: SearchOptions = {},
66: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
67:   // implementation
68: }
69: ```
70: 
71: ### Interface Documentation
72: 
73: ```typescript
74: /**
75:  * Configuration for trigger-index lookup operations.
76:  *
77:  * @remarks
78:  * All properties have sensible defaults. Only `query` is required
79:  * at the call site (passed as a separate parameter).
80:  */
81: interface SearchOptions {
82:   /** Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 10. */
83:   limit?: number;
84: 
85:   /** Filter results to a specific spec folder path. */
86:   specFolder?: string;
87: 
88:   /** Filter by specific anchor types (e.g., 'state', 'next-steps'). */
89:   anchors?: readonly string[];
90: 
91:   /** Include full content in results. Defaults to false. */
92:   includeContent?: boolean;
93: }
94: ```
95: 
96: ### Class Documentation
97: 
98: ```typescript
99: /**
100:  * Manages vector-based semantic search index.
101:  *
102:  * @remarks
103:  * Uses sqlite-vec for vector storage and cosine similarity search.
104:  * Must call {@link VectorIndex.initialize} before first use.
105:  *
106:  * @example
107:  * ```typescript
108:  * const index = new VectorIndex(dbPath);
109:  * await index.initialize();
110:  * const results = await index.search(embedding, { limit: 10 });
111:  * ```
112:  */
113: class VectorIndex {
114:   /**
115:    * Create a VectorIndex instance.
116:    *
117:    * @param dbPath - Path to SQLite database file
118:    * @param dimension - Vector dimension size (must match embedding model)
119:    */
120:   constructor(
121:     private readonly dbPath: string,
122:     private readonly dimension: number,
123:   ) { }
124: }
125: ```
126: 
127: ### Generic Type Documentation
128: 
129: ```typescript
130: /**
131:  * Cached value with TTL-based expiration.
132:  *
133:  * @typeParam T - The type of the cached value
134:  */
135: interface CacheEntry<T> {
136:   /** The cached value. */
137:   readonly value: T;
138: 
139:   /** Unix timestamp (ms) when this entry was created. */
140:   readonly createdAt: number;
141: 
142:   /** TTL in milliseconds. Entry expires at createdAt + ttl. */
143:   readonly ttl: number;
144: }
145: ```
146: 
147: ### TSDoc Tag Reference
148: 
149: | Tag             | Purpose                                      | Example                                        |
150: |-----------------|----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
151: | `@param`        | Describe parameter                           | `@param query - Search text`                   |
152: | `@returns`      | Describe return value                        | `@returns Array of results`                    |
153: | `@throws`       | Document thrown exceptions                   | `@throws {@link MemoryError} If DB fails`      |
154: | `@typeParam`    | Describe generic type parameter              | `@typeParam T - Cached value type`             |
155: | `@remarks`      | Extended description (after summary)         | `@remarks Uses cosine similarity...`           |
156: | `@example`      | Usage example with code block                | `@example \`\`\`typescript ... \`\`\``         |
157: | `@see`          | Cross-reference                              | `@see {@link SearchOptions}`                   |
158: | `@deprecated`   | Mark as deprecated                           | `@deprecated Use searchMemories instead`       |
159: | `@internal`     | Mark as internal (not public API)            | `@internal`                                    |
160: | `@readonly`     | Indicate read-only property                  | `@readonly`                                    |
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 3. TYPED ERROR CLASSES
165: 
166: ### Custom Error Pattern
167: 
168: Extend `Error` with typed properties:
169: 
170: ```typescript
171: import type { RecoveryHint } from './recovery-hints.js';
172: 
173: export const ErrorCodes = {
174:   INVALID_PARAMETER: 'E030',
175: } as const;
176: 
177: /**
178:  * Base error for all memory operations.
179:  */
180: class MemoryError extends Error {
181:   /** Error code for programmatic handling. */
182:   public code: string;
183: 
184:   /** Additional details for debugging. */
185:   public details: Record<string, unknown>;
186: 
187:   /** Optional recovery guidance for callers. */
188:   public recoveryHint?: RecoveryHint;
189: 
190:   constructor(
191:     code: string,
192:     message: string,
193:     details: Record<string, unknown> = {},
194:   ) {
195:     super(message);
196:     this.name = 'MemoryError';
197:     this.code = code;
198:     this.details = details;
199:     Object.setPrototypeOf(this, MemoryError.prototype);
200:   }
201: }
202: 
203: // Specialized error subclass
204: class ValidationError extends MemoryError {
205:   constructor(message: string, details: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
206:     super(ErrorCodes.INVALID_PARAMETER, message, details);
207:     this.name = 'ValidationError';
208:   }
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ### Error Code Const Object
213: 
214: ```typescript
215: export const ErrorCodes = {
216:   EMBEDDING_FAILED: 'E001',
217:   FILE_NOT_FOUND: 'E010',
218:   DB_CONNECTION_FAILED: 'E020',
219:   INVALID_PARAMETER: 'E030',
220:   SEARCH_FAILED: 'E040',
221:   RATE_LIMITED: 'E429',
222: } as const;
223: 
224: export type ErrorCodeKey = keyof typeof ErrorCodes;
225: ```
226: 
227: Prefer `export const X = {...} as const` plus `keyof typeof X` over `enum` for shared code maps.
228: 
229: ### Typed Error Handling
230: 
231: ```typescript
232: // Catching typed errors
233: try {
234:   await searchMemories(query, options);
235: } catch (error: unknown) {
236:   if (error instanceof MemoryError) {
237:     // TypeScript narrows to MemoryError — .code and .details available
238:     console.error(`[search] ${error.code}: ${error.message}`);
239:     if (error.code === ErrorCodes.SEARCH_FAILED) {
240:       // Handle timeout specifically
241:     }
242:   } else if (error instanceof Error) {
243:     console.error(`[search] Unexpected error: ${error.message}`);
244:   } else {
245:     console.error('[search] Unknown error:', error);
246:   }
247: }
248: ```
249: 
250: **Rule**: Always type `catch` parameter as `unknown` and narrow with `instanceof`.
251: 
252: ---
253: 
254: ## 4. ASYNC PATTERNS
255: 
256: ### Typed Promises
257: 
258: ```typescript
259: // Explicit return type for async functions
260: async function fetchMemories(
261:   query: string,
262: ): Promise<MemoryRecord[]> {
263:   const results = await database.search(query);
264:   return results;
265: }
266: ```
267: 
268: ### Parallel Operations
269: 
270: ```typescript
271: // Parallel execution with typed results
272: const [users, posts]: [User[], Post[]] = await Promise.all([
273:   fetchUsers(),
274:   fetchPosts(),
275: ]);
276: 
277: // Promise.allSettled for partial failure tolerance
278: const results = await Promise.allSettled([
279:   embedText(text1),
280:   embedText(text2),
281:   embedText(text3),
282: ]);
283: 
284: for (const result of results) {
285:   if (result.status === 'fulfilled') {
286:     processEmbedding(result.value);
287:   } else {
288:     console.error(`Embedding failed: ${result.reason}`);
289:   }
290: }
291: ```
292: 
293: ### Async Error Wrapper
294: 
295: ```typescript
296: // Generic async error wrapper with typed result
297: async function safeAsync<T>(
298:   fn: () => Promise<T>,
299:   context: string,
300: ): Promise<OperationResult<T>> {
301:   try {
302:     const data = await fn();
303:     return { success: true, data };
304:   } catch (error: unknown) {
305:     const message = error instanceof Error
306:       ? error.message
307:       : String(error);
308:     console.error(`[${context}] Failed: ${message}`);
309:     return { success: false, error: message, code: ErrorCodes.SEARCH_FAILED };
310:   }
311: }
312: 
313: // Usage
314: const result = await safeAsync(
315:   () => searchMemories(query),
316:   'memory-search',
317: );
318: ```
319: 
320: ---

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:

906: from pathlib import Path

911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:

915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")

929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```

932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory

937: - Framework: pytest

955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):

735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10

845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):

851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:

865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown

969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python

978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:

1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():

34: ## 2. IMPORT / EXPORT TEMPLATES

36: ### Import Ordering
37: 
38: ```typescript
39: // 1. Node.js built-ins
40: import fs from 'node:fs';
41: import path from 'node:path';
42: 
43: // 2. Third-party
44: import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
45: import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js';
46: 
47: // 3. Local modules
48: import { loadConfig } from './core/config.js';
49: import { MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';

51: // 4. Type-only imports (grouped together)
52: import type { SearchOptions, SearchResult } from '../types.js';
53: import type { DatabaseConfig } from './core/config.js';
54: ```
55: 
56: Under `module: "nodenext"`, source files stay `.ts`, but relative import specifiers use the emitted `.js` extension. Use the `node:` prefix for built-in modules.

58: ### Export Patterns
59: 
60: ```typescript
61: // Named exports (preferred)
62: export function search(query: string): SearchResult[] { }
63: export class VectorIndex { }
64: export const MAX_RESULTS = 100;
65: 
66: // Type-only exports
67: export type { SearchResult, SearchOptions };

69: // Barrel file (index.ts)

71: export { VectorIndex } from './search/vector-index.js';
72: export type { SearchResult } from '../types.js';
73: 
74: // Default export (use sparingly — named exports preferred)
75: export default class ContextServer { }
76: 
77: // Re-export everything from a module
78: export * from './module.js';

192: const limit: number | undefined = options.limit;
193: const result: MemoryRecord | null = findById(id);
194: ```
195: 
196: ### Function Signatures
197: 
198: ```typescript
199: // Named function
200: function add(a: number, b: number): number {
201:   return a + b;
202: }
203: 
204: // Arrow function
205: const multiply = (a: number, b: number): number => a * b;
206: 
207: // Async function
208: async function fetch(id: string): Promise<MemoryRecord | null> {
209:   return database.get(id);
210: }
211: 
212: // Optional parameters
213: function search(query: string, limit?: number): SearchResult[] { }
214: 
215: // Default parameters
216: function configure(options: Partial<Config> = {}): Config { }
217: 
218: // Rest parameters
219: function log(prefix: string, ...args: unknown[]): void { }
220: 
221: // Type guard
222: function isString(value: unknown): value is string {
223:   return typeof value === 'string';
224: }
225: ```
226: 
227: ### Object and Array Types
228: 
229: ```typescript
230: // Object type with readonly
231: interface Config {
232:   readonly host: string;
233:   readonly port: number;
234:   debug?: boolean;  // optional
235: }
236: 
237: // Array types
238: const ids: string[] = [];
239: const matrix: number[][] = [];
240: const records: readonly MemoryRecord[] = [];  // immutable array
241: 
242: // Tuple
243: const pair: [string, number] = ['score', 0.95];
244: ```
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: ## 6. COMMON UTILITY TYPE PATTERNS
249: 
250: ```typescript
251: // Partial — all properties optional (for updates/overrides)
252: function updateConfig(overrides: Partial<SearchConfig>): SearchConfig {
253:   return { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...overrides };
254: }
255: 
256: // Required — all properties required (for validated state)
257: function validate(input: Partial<Config>): Required<Config> {
258:   // ... validation logic
259: }
260: 
261: // Pick — select specific properties
262: type MemorySummary = Pick<MemoryRecord, 'id' | 'text' | 'score'>;
263: 
264: // Omit — exclude properties
265: type PublicRecord = Omit<MemoryRecord, 'internalScore' | 'rawEmbedding'>;
266: 
267: // Record — typed key-value object
268: const scores: Record<string, number> = { relevance: 0.9, recency: 0.7 };
269: 
270: // Readonly — immutable version
271: const frozen: Readonly<Config> = Object.freeze(config);
272: 
273: // NonNullable — strip null/undefined
274: type ValidId = NonNullable<string | null | undefined>;  // string
275: 
276: // ReturnType — extract return type from function
277: type SearchReturn = ReturnType<typeof searchMemories>;
278: ```

15: 
16: Copy-paste templates, naming cheat sheet, and common patterns for TypeScript development in OpenCode.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Quick-access reference card for TypeScript patterns. For detailed explanations, see:
25: - [style-guide.md](../style-guide/overview-strict-and-naming.md) - Full style documentation
26: - [quality-standards.md](../quality-standards/overview-and-type-system.md) - Quality requirements

30: settings are only fallback defaults for workspaces that do not override them.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Starting a TypeScript file from the standard template
35: - Looking up naming or type-annotation conventions
36: - Reusing common TypeScript utility-type patterns
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. COMPLETE FILE TEMPLATE
41: 
42: ```typescript
43: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44: // MODULE: [Module Name]
45: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46: 
47: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
48: // 1. IMPORTS
49: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50: 
51: import fs from 'node:fs';
52: import path from 'node:path';
53: 
54: import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
55: 
56: import { loadConfig } from './core/config.js';
57: import { ErrorCodes, MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
58: 
59: import type { SearchOptions, SearchResult } from '../types.js';
60: 
61: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
62: // 2. TYPE DEFINITIONS
63: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
64: 
65: /** Configuration for the main operation. */
66: interface ModuleConfig {
67:   readonly timeout: number;
68:   readonly maxRetries: number;
69:   readonly verbose: boolean;
70: }
71: 
72: /** Possible operation outcomes. */
73: type OperationOutcome = 'success' | 'failure' | 'timeout';
74: 
75: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
76: // 3. CONSTANTS
77: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78: 
79: const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 5_000;
80: const MAX_RETRIES = 3;
81: const DEFAULT_ERROR_DETAILS = Object.freeze({
82:   source: 'module-name',
83: } satisfies Record<string, unknown>);
84: 
85: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86: // 4. HELPERS
87: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
88: 
89: function validateInput(input: unknown): input is string {
90:   return typeof input === 'string' && input.length > 0;
91: }
92: 
93: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
94: // 5. CORE LOGIC
95: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
96: 
97: /**
98:  * Main function description.
99:  *
100:  * @param input - Input description
101:  * @param options - Configuration options
102:  * @returns Result object with success status and data
103:  * @throws {@link MemoryError} If operation fails
104:  */
105: export async function mainFunction(
106:   input: string,
107:   options: Partial<ModuleConfig> = {},
108: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
109:   if (!validateInput(input)) {
110:     throw new MemoryError(
111:       ErrorCodes.INVALID_PARAMETER,
112:       'Invalid input: expected non-empty string',
113:       DEFAULT_ERROR_DETAILS,
114:     );
115:   }
116: 
117:   try {
118:     const config: ModuleConfig = {
119:       timeout: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
120:       maxRetries: MAX_RETRIES,
121:       verbose: false,
122:       ...options,
123:     };
124:     const result = await process(input, config);
125:     return result;
126:   } catch (error: unknown) {
127:     const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
128:     console.error(`[module-name] Error: ${message}`);
129:     throw error;
130:   }
131: }
132: 
133: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
134: // 6. EXPORTS
135: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
136: 
137: export { validateInput };
138: export type { ModuleConfig, OperationOutcome };
139: ```
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## 3. NAMING CHEAT SHEET
144: 
145: | Element           | Convention         | Example                   |
146: |-------------------|--------------------|---------------------------|
147: | Functions         | `camelCase`        | `loadConfig`              |
148: | Constants         | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `MAX_RETRIES`             |
149: | Classes           | `PascalCase`       | `MemoryError`             |
150: | Interfaces        | `PascalCase`       | `SearchResult`            |
151: | Type aliases      | `PascalCase`       | `MemoryState`             |
152: | Const maps        | `PascalCase`       | `ErrorCodes`              |
153: | Const map keys    | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `ErrorCodes.INVALID_PARAMETER` |
154: | Generics          | `T`-prefix         | `<T>`, `<TResult>`        |
155: | Local variables   | `camelCase`        | `searchResults`           |
156: | Module variables  | `camelCase`        | `dbConnection`            |
157: | Parameters        | `camelCase`        | `queryText`               |
158: | Booleans          | `is`/`has`/`can`   | `isValid`, `hasItems`     |
159: | Files             | `kebab-case`       | `memory-search.ts`        |
160: | Private members   | `_prefix`          | `private _connection`     |
161: 
162: **Legacy exception**: `IEmbeddingProvider` and `IVectorStore` keep `I` prefix. New interfaces omit it.
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## 4. SECTION ORDERING
167: 
168: ```
169: 1. IMPORTS           (Node built-ins, third-party, local, type-only)
170: 2. TYPE DEFINITIONS  (Interfaces, types, const-derived unions)
171: 3. CONSTANTS         (Configuration values)
172: 4. HELPERS           (Internal utility functions)
173: 5. CORE LOGIC        (Main implementation)
174: 6. EXPORTS           (Module public interface)
175: ```
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## 5. TYPE ANNOTATION PATTERNS
180: 
181: ### Basic Annotations
182: 
183: ```typescript
184: // Variables
185: const name: string = 'hello';
186: const count: number = 42;
187: const isActive: boolean = true;
188: const items: string[] = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
189: const metadata: Record<string, unknown> = {};
190: 
191: // Optional
192: const limit: number | undefined = options.limit;
193: const result: MemoryRecord | null = findById(id);
194: ```
195: 
196: ### Function Signatures
197: 
198: ```typescript
199: // Named function
200: function add(a: number, b: number): number {
201:   return a + b;
202: }
203: 
204: // Arrow function
205: const multiply = (a: number, b: number): number => a * b;
206: 
207: // Async function
208: async function fetch(id: string): Promise<MemoryRecord | null> {
209:   return database.get(id);
210: }
211: 
212: // Optional parameters
213: function search(query: string, limit?: number): SearchResult[] { }
214: 
215: // Default parameters
216: function configure(options: Partial<Config> = {}): Config { }
217: 
218: // Rest parameters
219: function log(prefix: string, ...args: unknown[]): void { }
220: 
221: // Type guard
222: function isString(value: unknown): value is string {
223:   return typeof value === 'string';
224: }
225: ```
226: 
227: ### Object and Array Types
228: 
229: ```typescript
230: // Object type with readonly
231: interface Config {
232:   readonly host: string;
233:   readonly port: number;
234:   debug?: boolean;  // optional
235: }
236: 
237: // Array types
238: const ids: string[] = [];
239: const matrix: number[][] = [];
240: const records: readonly MemoryRecord[] = [];  // immutable array
241: 
242: // Tuple
243: const pair: [string, number] = ['score', 0.95];
244: ```
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: ## 6. COMMON UTILITY TYPE PATTERNS
249: 
250: ```typescript
251: // Partial — all properties optional (for updates/overrides)
252: function updateConfig(overrides: Partial<SearchConfig>): SearchConfig {
253:   return { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...overrides };
254: }
255: 
256: // Required — all properties required (for validated state)
257: function validate(input: Partial<Config>): Required<Config> {
258:   // ... validation logic
259: }
260: 
261: // Pick — select specific properties
262: type MemorySummary = Pick<MemoryRecord, 'id' | 'text' | 'score'>;
263: 
264: // Omit — exclude properties
265: type PublicRecord = Omit<MemoryRecord, 'internalScore' | 'rawEmbedding'>;
266: 
267: // Record — typed key-value object
268: const scores: Record<string, number> = { relevance: 0.9, recency: 0.7 };
269: 
270: // Readonly — immutable version
271: const frozen: Readonly<Config> = Object.freeze(config);

274: type ValidId = NonNullable<string | null | undefined>;  // string

14: # Formatting, Imports, Commenting & JS/TS Coexistence
15: 
16: Formatting, import, commenting, and mixed JavaScript/TypeScript guidance for OpenCode packages.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines TypeScript formatting, import, commenting, and JavaScript coexistence conventions.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - Formatting TypeScript or organizing imports
29: - Writing durable TypeScript comments and TSDoc
30: - Integrating JavaScript modules into TypeScript packages
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. FORMATTING RULES
35: 
36: ### Indentation
37: 
38: - **Size**: 2 spaces (same as JavaScript)
39: - **Tabs**: Never use tabs
40: 
41: ### Braces
42: 
43: **Style**: K&R (opening brace on same line)
44: 
45: ```typescript
46: if (condition) {
47:   // code
48: } else {
49:   // code
50: }
51: 
52: function example(): void {
53:   // code
54: }
55: ```
56: 
57: ### Semicolons
58: 
59: **Rule**: Always use semicolons (same as JavaScript)
60: 
61: ```typescript
62: const value: number = 42;
63: return result;
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Quotes
67: 
68: **Rule**: Single quotes for strings (same as JavaScript)
69: 
70: ```typescript
71: const message = 'Hello world';
72: const template = `Value: ${value}`;  // Template literals OK
73: ```
74: 
75: ### Line Length
76: 
77: - **Maximum**: 100 characters
78: - **Preferred**: 80 characters
79: - **Exception**: URLs, long type signatures, and import paths
80: 
81: ### Type Annotation Placement
82: 
83: **Rule**: Type annotations follow the colon with a single space.
84: 
85: ```typescript
86: // CORRECT
87: const name: string = 'hello';
88: function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }
89: const items: string[] = [];
90: 
91: // INCORRECT
92: const name:string = 'hello';           // no space after colon
93: const name :string = 'hello';          // space before colon
94: ```
95: 
96: ### Multiline Type Definitions
97: 
98: For types that exceed line length limits, break at logical points:
99: 
100: ```typescript
101: // Short — single line is fine
102: interface Point { x: number; y: number; }
103: 
104: // Medium — use multiline formatting
105: interface SearchConfig {
106:   readonly query: string;
107:   readonly limit: number;
108:   readonly offset: number;
109:   readonly filters: Record<string, unknown>;
110: }
111: 
112: // Long union types — one member per line
113: type MemoryOperation =
114:   | 'save'
115:   | 'search'
116:   | 'delete'
117:   | 'archive'
118:   | 'consolidate';
119: 
120: // Long function types — break parameters
121: type TransformFn = (
122:   input: string,
123:   options: TransformOptions,
124:   context: ExecutionContext,
125: ) => Promise<TransformResult>;
126: ```
127: 
128: ### Trailing Commas
129: 
130: **Rule**: Use trailing commas in multiline constructs (arrays, objects, parameters, type members).
131: 
132: ```typescript
133: // CORRECT — trailing comma
134: const config: SearchConfig = {
135:   query: 'test',
136:   limit: 10,
137:   offset: 0,
138: };
139: 
140: // CORRECT — trailing comma in multiline parameters
141: function search(
142:   query: string,
143:   options: SearchOptions,
144:   context: ExecutionContext,
145: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
146:   // ...
147: }
148: ```
149: 
150: ---
151: 
152: ## 3. IMPORT ORDERING
153: 
154: ### Four-Group Import Order
155: 
156: TypeScript imports follow a four-group ordering with blank lines between groups:
157: 
158: ```typescript
159: // 1. Node.js built-in modules
160: import fs from 'node:fs';
161: import path from 'node:path';
162: 
163: // 2. Third-party packages
164: import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js';
165: import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
166: 
167: // 3. Local modules (project code)
168: import { loadConfig } from './core/config.js';
169: import { MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
170: import { validateInputLengths } from './utils/validation.js';
171: 
172: // 4. Type-only imports (grouped together)
173: import type { SearchOptions, SearchResult } from '../types.js';
174: import type { DatabaseConfig } from './core/config.js';
175: ```
176: 
177: Under `module: "nodenext"`, TypeScript source remains `.ts`, but every relative import specifier must use the emitted `.js` extension. Built-in modules use the `node:` protocol prefix.
178: 
179: ### Type-Only Imports
180: 
181: Use `import type` for imports used only in type positions. This ensures they are erased at compile time and do not create runtime dependencies. Group type-only imports together; do not interleave value and type imports from the same module.
182: 
183: ```typescript
184: // CORRECT — type-only import (erased at compile time)
185: import type { EmbeddingProfile } from '../shared/types.js';
186: 
187: // CORRECT — mixed: value import (needed at runtime)
188: import { MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
189: 
190: // INCORRECT — importing a type without `import type`
191: import { SearchResult } from '../types.js';  // Only used as a type
192: ```
193: 
194: **Rule**: If an import is ONLY used in type annotations, parameter types, return types, or generic constraints, use `import type`.
195: 
196: ### Re-export Syntax
197: 
198: ```typescript
199: // Re-export everything
200: export * from './module.js';
201: 
202: // Re-export specific items
203: export { ErrorCodes, MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
204: 
205: // Re-export types only
206: export type { SearchResult, SearchOptions } from '../types.js';
207: ```
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: ## 4. COMMENTING RULES
212: 
213: ### Principles (Same as JavaScript)
214: 
215: 1. **Quantity limit (Skilled surface setting)**: Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines of code, this surface's budget for the shared comment-density rule (see [naming and commenting](../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md))
216: 2. **Focus on purposeful semantics**: Explain WHY something is done, not WHAT it does
217: 3. **Focus on WHY, not WHAT**: Explain intent, constraints, reasoning
218: 4. **No commented-out code**: Delete unused code (git preserves history)
219: 
220: ### Comment Examples
221: 
222: Use plain comments that explain reasoning:
223: 
224: - `// Rationale for this path`
225: - `// Contract/precondition that must hold`
226: - `// State that must hold after execution`
227: - `// SEC: security note tied to a stable standard (CWE-###)`
228: - `// Reliability/performance/security risk control`
229: - No spec-folder-internal ids (`T###`/`REQ-###`/`CHK-###`/ADR/ticket) in comments — see [`../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md`](../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md) §4.
230: 
231: ### Capitalization
232: 
233: All comment text MUST start with a capital letter:
234: 
235: ```typescript
236: // Reverse order preserves dependency chain     // correct
237: // reverse order preserves dependency chain     // wrong
238: ```
239: 
240: **Exceptions**: `eslint-disable` directives, `@ts-` annotations, and inline code references.
241: 
242: ### TSDoc Comments (Replaces JSDoc)
243: 
244: TypeScript uses TSDoc format for documentation comments. See `quality-standards.md` for the full TSDoc reference.
245: 
246: ```typescript
247: /**
248:  * Look up trigger-index entries matching a query.
249:  *
250:  * @param query - Search query text
251:  * @param options - Lookup configuration
252:  * @returns Array of matching trigger entries
253:  * @throws {@link SpecFolderError} If the spec folder cannot be resolved
254:  */
255: async function lookupTriggers(
256:   query: string,
257:   options: SearchOptions = {},
258: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
259:   // implementation
260: }
261: ```
262: 
263: **Key difference from JSDoc**: TSDoc does not use `{type}` annotations in tags because TypeScript has native type annotations. Compare:
264: 
265: ```typescript
266: // JSDoc (JavaScript) — types in comments
267: /** @param {string} query - Search text */
268: 
269: // TSDoc (TypeScript) — types in code
270: /** @param query - Search text */
271: function search(query: string): void { }
272: ```
273: 
274: ---
275: 
276: ## 5. MIXED JS/TS COEXISTENCE PATTERNS
277: 
278: During the transitional period where the codebase contains both JavaScript and TypeScript files, the following patterns are acceptable.
279: 
280: ### TypeScript Importing JavaScript
281: 
282: Use ESM imports for local modules and keep the emitted `.js` extension in the specifier. For CommonJS-only packages or modules, create a scoped `require` with `createRequire(import.meta.url)`; bare `require(...)` is a runtime `ReferenceError` in ESM even when `tsc` accepts it.
283: 
284: ```typescript
285: // Option A — local JS module through ESM
286: import config from './legacy-config.js';
287: 
288: // Option B — CommonJS-only dependency
289: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
290: 
291: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
292: const legacyHelper = require('legacy-helper') as LegacyHelper;
293: ```
294: 
295: For frequently imported JS modules, add a `.d.ts` declaration file co-located with the JS module and sharing its exact basename. A relative `declare module './legacy-config.js' { ... }` block does NOT type an untyped local sibling — it fails with `TS7016 (Could not find a declaration file for module …)`; use plain top-level declarations instead:
296: 
297: ```typescript
298: // legacy-config.d.ts — same directory and exact basename as legacy-config.js
299: export interface LegacyConfig {
300:   version: string;
301:   features: string[];
302: }
303: declare const config: LegacyConfig;
304: export default config;
305: ```
306: 
307: ### Dynamic require() with try-catch
308: 
309: For optional dependencies (e.g., native modules that may not be installed):
310: 
311: ```typescript
312: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
313: 
314: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
315: 
316: let sqliteVec: any;
317: try {
318:   // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires
319:   sqliteVec = require('sqlite-vec');
320: } catch {
321:   console.warn('[vector-index] sqlite-vec not available, falling back');
322:   sqliteVec = null;
323: }
324: ```
325: 
326: ### 'use strict' Rule
327: 
328: - `.js` files: **ALWAYS** include `'use strict';` at the top
329: - `.ts` files: **NEVER** include `'use strict';` (tsconfig `strict: true` handles it)
330: 
331: ### Backward-Compatible Export Aliases
332: 
333: During migration, modules may export both old (`snake_case`) and new (`camelCase`) names:
334: 
335: ```typescript
336: // Primary exports
337: export { triggerLookup, loadConfig };
338: 
339: // Backward-compatible aliases — remove after migration completes
340: export {
341:   triggerLookup as trigger_lookup,
342:   loadConfig as load_config,
343: };
344: ```
345: 
346: ### allowJs in tsconfig
347: 
348: When a TypeScript project includes legacy `.js` files that cannot be immediately converted:
349: 
350: ```jsonc
351: {
352:   "compilerOptions": {
353:     "allowJs": true,        // Include .js files in compilation
354:     "checkJs": false         // Don't type-check .js files (too noisy during migration)
355:   }
356: }
357: ```
358: 
359: Set `checkJs: true` only after the majority of JS files have been migrated or typed.
360:

14: # Formatting, Imports, Commenting & JS/TS Coexistence
15: 
16: Formatting, import, commenting, and mixed JavaScript/TypeScript guidance for OpenCode packages.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines TypeScript formatting, import, commenting, and JavaScript coexistence conventions.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - Formatting TypeScript or organizing imports
29: - Writing durable TypeScript comments and TSDoc
30: - Integrating JavaScript modules into TypeScript packages
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. FORMATTING RULES
35: 
36: ### Indentation
37: 
38: - **Size**: 2 spaces (same as JavaScript)
39: - **Tabs**: Never use tabs
40: 
41: ### Braces
42: 
43: **Style**: K&R (opening brace on same line)
44: 
45: ```typescript
46: if (condition) {
47:   // code
48: } else {
49:   // code
50: }
51: 
52: function example(): void {
53:   // code
54: }
55: ```
56: 
57: ### Semicolons
58: 
59: **Rule**: Always use semicolons (same as JavaScript)
60: 
61: ```typescript
62: const value: number = 42;
63: return result;
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Quotes
67: 
68: **Rule**: Single quotes for strings (same as JavaScript)
69: 
70: ```typescript
71: const message = 'Hello world';
72: const template = `Value: ${value}`;  // Template literals OK
73: ```
74: 
75: ### Line Length
76: 
77: - **Maximum**: 100 characters
78: - **Preferred**: 80 characters
79: - **Exception**: URLs, long type signatures, and import paths
80: 
81: ### Type Annotation Placement
82: 
83: **Rule**: Type annotations follow the colon with a single space.
84: 
85: ```typescript
86: // CORRECT
87: const name: string = 'hello';
88: function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }
89: const items: string[] = [];
90: 
91: // INCORRECT
92: const name:string = 'hello';           // no space after colon
93: const name :string = 'hello';          // space before colon
94: ```
95: 
96: ### Multiline Type Definitions
97: 
98: For types that exceed line length limits, break at logical points:
99: 
100: ```typescript
101: // Short — single line is fine
102: interface Point { x: number; y: number; }
103: 
104: // Medium — use multiline formatting
105: interface SearchConfig {
106:   readonly query: string;
107:   readonly limit: number;
108:   readonly offset: number;
109:   readonly filters: Record<string, unknown>;
110: }
111: 
112: // Long union types — one member per line
113: type MemoryOperation =
114:   | 'save'
115:   | 'search'
116:   | 'delete'
117:   | 'archive'
118:   | 'consolidate';
119: 
120: // Long function types — break parameters
121: type TransformFn = (
122:   input: string,
123:   options: TransformOptions,
124:   context: ExecutionContext,
125: ) => Promise<TransformResult>;
126: ```
127: 
128: ### Trailing Commas
129: 
130: **Rule**: Use trailing commas in multiline constructs (arrays, objects, parameters, type members).
131: 
132: ```typescript
133: // CORRECT — trailing comma
134: const config: SearchConfig = {
135:   query: 'test',
136:   limit: 10,
137:   offset: 0,
138: };
139: 
140: // CORRECT — trailing comma in multiline parameters
141: function search(
142:   query: string,
143:   options: SearchOptions,
144:   context: ExecutionContext,
145: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
146:   // ...
147: }
148: ```
149: 
150: ---
151: 
152: ## 3. IMPORT ORDERING
153: 
154: ### Four-Group Import Order
155: 
156: TypeScript imports follow a four-group ordering with blank lines between groups:
157: 
158: ```typescript
159: // 1. Node.js built-in modules
160: import fs from 'node:fs';
161: import path from 'node:path';
162: 
163: // 2. Third-party packages
164: import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js';
165: import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
166: 
167: // 3. Local modules (project code)
168: import { loadConfig } from './core/config.js';
169: import { MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
170: import { validateInputLengths } from './utils/validation.js';
171: 
172: // 4. Type-only imports (grouped together)
173: import type { SearchOptions, SearchResult } from '../types.js';
174: import type { DatabaseConfig } from './core/config.js';
175: ```
176: 
177: Under `module: "nodenext"`, TypeScript source remains `.ts`, but every relative import specifier must use the emitted `.js` extension. Built-in modules use the `node:` protocol prefix.
178: 
179: ### Type-Only Imports
180: 
181: Use `import type` for imports used only in type positions. This ensures they are erased at compile time and do not create runtime dependencies. Group type-only imports together; do not interleave value and type imports from the same module.
182: 
183: ```typescript
184: // CORRECT — type-only import (erased at compile time)
185: import type { EmbeddingProfile } from '../shared/types.js';
186: 
187: // CORRECT — mixed: value import (needed at runtime)
188: import { MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
189: 
190: // INCORRECT — importing a type without `import type`
191: import { SearchResult } from '../types.js';  // Only used as a type
192: ```
193: 
194: **Rule**: If an import is ONLY used in type annotations, parameter types, return types, or generic constraints, use `import type`.
195: 
196: ### Re-export Syntax
197: 
198: ```typescript
199: // Re-export everything
200: export * from './module.js';
201: 
202: // Re-export specific items
203: export { ErrorCodes, MemoryError } from './errors/core.js';
204: 
205: // Re-export types only
206: export type { SearchResult, SearchOptions } from '../types.js';
207: ```
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: ## 4. COMMENTING RULES
212: 
213: ### Principles (Same as JavaScript)
214: 
215: 1. **Quantity limit (Skilled surface setting)**: Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines of code, this surface's budget for the shared comment-density rule (see [naming and commenting](../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md))
216: 2. **Focus on purposeful semantics**: Explain WHY something is done, not WHAT it does
217: 3. **Focus on WHY, not WHAT**: Explain intent, constraints, reasoning
218: 4. **No commented-out code**: Delete unused code (git preserves history)
219: 
220: ### Comment Examples
221: 
222: Use plain comments that explain reasoning:
223: 
224: - `// Rationale for this path`
225: - `// Contract/precondition that must hold`
226: - `// State that must hold after execution`
227: - `// SEC: security note tied to a stable standard (CWE-###)`
228: - `// Reliability/performance/security risk control`
229: - No spec-folder-internal ids (`T###`/`REQ-###`/`CHK-###`/ADR/ticket) in comments — see [`../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md`](../../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md) §4.
230: 
231: ### Capitalization
232: 
233: All comment text MUST start with a capital letter:
234: 
235: ```typescript
236: // Reverse order preserves dependency chain     // correct
237: // reverse order preserves dependency chain     // wrong
238: ```
239: 
240: **Exceptions**: `eslint-disable` directives, `@ts-` annotations, and inline code references.
241: 
242: ### TSDoc Comments (Replaces JSDoc)
243: 
244: TypeScript uses TSDoc format for documentation comments. See `quality-standards.md` for the full TSDoc reference.
245: 
246: ```typescript
247: /**
248:  * Look up trigger-index entries matching a query.
249:  *
250:  * @param query - Search query text
251:  * @param options - Lookup configuration
252:  * @returns Array of matching trigger entries
253:  * @throws {@link SpecFolderError} If the spec folder cannot be resolved
254:  */
255: async function lookupTriggers(
256:   query: string,
257:   options: SearchOptions = {},
258: ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
259:   // implementation
260: }
261: ```
262: 
263: **Key difference from JSDoc**: TSDoc does not use `{type}` annotations in tags because TypeScript has native type annotations. Compare:
264: 
265: ```typescript
266: // JSDoc (JavaScript) — types in comments
267: /** @param {string} query - Search text */
268: 
269: // TSDoc (TypeScript) — types in code
270: /** @param query - Search text */
271: function search(query: string): void { }
272: ```
273: 
274: ---
275: 
276: ## 5. MIXED JS/TS COEXISTENCE PATTERNS
277: 
278: During the transitional period where the codebase contains both JavaScript and TypeScript files, the following patterns are acceptable.
279: 
280: ### TypeScript Importing JavaScript
281: 
282: Use ESM imports for local modules and keep the emitted `.js` extension in the specifier. For CommonJS-only packages or modules, create a scoped `require` with `createRequire(import.meta.url)`; bare `require(...)` is a runtime `ReferenceError` in ESM even when `tsc` accepts it.
283: 
284: ```typescript
285: // Option A — local JS module through ESM
286: import config from './legacy-config.js';
287: 
288: // Option B — CommonJS-only dependency
289: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
290: 
291: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
292: const legacyHelper = require('legacy-helper') as LegacyHelper;
293: ```
294: 
295: For frequently imported JS modules, add a `.d.ts` declaration file co-located with the JS module and sharing its exact basename. A relative `declare module './legacy-config.js' { ... }` block does NOT type an untyped local sibling — it fails with `TS7016 (Could not find a declaration file for module …)`; use plain top-level declarations instead:
296: 
297: ```typescript
298: // legacy-config.d.ts — same directory and exact basename as legacy-config.js
299: export interface LegacyConfig {
300:   version: string;
301:   features: string[];
302: }
303: declare const config: LegacyConfig;
304: export default config;
305: ```
306: 
307: ### Dynamic require() with try-catch
308: 
309: For optional dependencies (e.g., native modules that may not be installed):
310: 
311: ```typescript
312: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
313: 
314: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
315: 
316: let sqliteVec: any;
317: try {
318:   // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires
319:   sqliteVec = require('sqlite-vec');
320: } catch {
321:   console.warn('[vector-index] sqlite-vec not available, falling back');
322:   sqliteVec = null;
323: }
324: ```
325: 
326: ### 'use strict' Rule
327: 
328: - `.js` files: **ALWAYS** include `'use strict';` at the top
329: - `.ts` files: **NEVER** include `'use strict';` (tsconfig `strict: true` handles it)
330: 
331: ### Backward-Compatible Export Aliases
332: 
333: During migration, modules may export both old (`snake_case`) and new (`camelCase`) names:
334: 
335: ```typescript
336: // Primary exports
337: export { triggerLookup, loadConfig };
338: 
339: // Backward-compatible aliases — remove after migration completes
340: export {
341:   triggerLookup as trigger_lookup,
342:   loadConfig as load_config,
343: };
344: ```
345: 
346: ### allowJs in tsconfig
347: 
348: When a TypeScript project includes legacy `.js` files that cannot be immediately converted:
349: 
350: ```jsonc
351: {
352:   "compilerOptions": {
353:     "allowJs": true,        // Include .js files in compilation
354:     "checkJs": false         // Don't type-check .js files (too noisy during migration)
355:   }
356: }
357: ```
358: 
359: Set `checkJs: true` only after the majority of JS files have been migrated or typed.
360: 
361: ---
362:

14: # TypeScript Style Guide
15: 
16: Formatting standards and naming conventions for TypeScript files in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines consistent styling rules for TypeScript files to ensure readability, maintainability, and alignment across all OpenCode TypeScript code.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - Writing new TypeScript files
29: - Reviewing TypeScript code for consistency
30: - Resolving style disagreements in code review
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. FILE HEADER FORMAT
35: 
36: All TypeScript files MUST begin with a module header block identifying the module.
37: 
38: ### Template
39: 
40: ```typescript
41: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
42: // MODULE: [Module Name]
43: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44: ```
45: 
46: ### Requirements
47: 
48: - Box width: 67 characters total (box-drawing line)
49: - Module name: Left-aligned within header block
50: - No `'use strict'` directive required (TypeScript `strict` mode in tsconfig replaces it)
51: - Immediately followed by imports
52: 
53: **Rationale**: TypeScript's `"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json` enables strict
54: type checking at compilation. Current system-spec-kit workspaces are
55: package-aware: `shared/` and `mcp-server/` use NodeNext ESM, `scripts/` uses
56: ES2022 ESM, and the root CommonJS setting is only a fallback default.
57: 
58: ### Full Header Example
59: 
60: ```typescript
61: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
62: // MODULE: Memory Search Handler
63: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
64: 
65: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66: // 1. IMPORTS
67: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
68: 
69: import path from 'node:path';
70: 
71: import type { SearchOptions } from '../types.js';
72: ```
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 3. STRICT MODE
77: 
78: ### tsconfig.json Replaces 'use strict'
79: 
80: In JavaScript `.js/.cjs`, files require `'use strict';` at the top. In
81: TypeScript, the `tsconfig.json` setting `"strict": true` enforces type-system
82: strictness at the compiler level, while ESM workspaces are strict by runtime
83: semantics.
84: 
85: ```jsonc
86: // tsconfig.json
87: {
88:   "compilerOptions": {
89:     "strict": true  // Enables all strict type-checking options
90:   }
91: }
92: ```
93: 
94: **What `strict: true` enables:**
95: - `strictNullChecks` - null/undefined handled explicitly
96: - `strictFunctionTypes` - stricter function parameter checking
97: - `strictBindCallApply` - stricter bind/call/apply checking
98: - `strictPropertyInitialization` - class properties must be initialized
99: - `noImplicitAny` - parameters and variables must have types
100: - `noImplicitThis` - `this` must have explicit type
101: - `alwaysStrict` - parses source in strict mode and emits strict markers where the selected module target requires them
102: 
103: **Rule**: Do NOT add `'use strict';` to TypeScript source files. Use the module
104: format selected by the owning package (`nodenext`, `es2022`, or inherited
105: fallback).
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## 4. SECTION ORGANIZATION
110: 
111: Large files are organized using numbered section dividers, consistent with JavaScript style.
112: 
113: ### Section Divider Templates
114: 
115: Two formats are acceptable. Use either consistently within a single file.
116: 
117: **Format A — Line-comment dividers** (used in most files):
118: 
119: ```typescript
120: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
121: // 1. [SECTION NAME]
122: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
123: ```
124: 
125: **Format B — Block-comment dividers** (used in 27+ files across the codebase):
126: 
127: ```typescript
128: /* ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
129:    1. SECTION NAME
130: ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
131: ```
132: 
133: Both formats serve the same purpose: visual separation of major code sections with numbered headings. Choose one format per file and apply it consistently.
134: 
135: ### Standard Section Order
136: 
137: | Order | Section Name      | Purpose                                |
138: |-------|-------------------|----------------------------------------|
139: | 1     | IMPORTS           | Module dependencies (with type imports)|
140: | 2     | TYPE DEFINITIONS  | Interfaces, types, const-derived unions|
141: | 3     | CONSTANTS         | Configuration values, magic numbers    |
142: | 4     | HELPERS           | Internal utility functions              |
143: | 5     | CORE LOGIC        | Main implementation                    |
144: | 6     | EXPORTS           | Module public interface                |
145: 
146: **Key difference from JavaScript**: TypeScript files include a TYPE DEFINITIONS section (section 2) between imports and constants. This is where interfaces, type aliases, and const-derived unions are defined.
147: 
148: Number sections from the first divider actually present in the file. File headers and module banners do not count, so a file whose first numbered divider is `TYPE DEFINITIONS` should label that divider `1`, not `2`.
149: 
150: ### TYPE DEFINITIONS Section Example (when IMPORTS is present as section 1)
151: 
152: ```typescript
153: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
154: // 2. TYPE DEFINITIONS
155: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
156: 
157: /** Configuration for search operations. */
158: interface SearchConfig {
159:   readonly maxResults: number;
160:   readonly timeout: number;
161:   readonly includeMetadata: boolean;
162: }
163: 
164: /** Possible states for a memory entry. */
165: type MemoryState = 'active' | 'archived' | 'pending';
166: 
167: /** Error codes for memory operations. */
168: const ErrorCodes = {
169:   NOT_FOUND: 'NOT_FOUND',
170:   TIMEOUT: 'TIMEOUT',
171:   CONNECTION_FAILED: 'CONNECTION_FAILED',
172: } as const;
173: 
174: type ErrorCodeKey = keyof typeof ErrorCodes;
175: ```
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## 5. NAMING CONVENTIONS
180: 
181: ### Interface Names
182: 
183: **Style**: `PascalCase` (no `I` prefix for new interfaces)
184: 
185: ```typescript
186: // CORRECT — new interfaces
187: interface SearchResult { }
188: interface EmbeddingProvider { }
189: interface MemoryRecord { }
190: 
191: // CORRECT — legacy exception (documented below)
192: interface IEmbeddingProvider { }
193: interface IVectorStore { }
194: 
195: // INCORRECT
196: interface iSearchResult { }      // camelCase
197: interface search_result { }      // snake_case
198: interface ISearchResult { }      // I prefix on new interface
199: ```
200: 
201: **Legacy Exception**: `IEmbeddingProvider` and `IVectorStore` retain their `I` prefix for backward compatibility with re-export aliases across the codebase. All NEW interfaces omit the prefix. This exception is documented in the migration plan (Decision D5).
202: 
203: ### Type Alias Names
204: 
205: **Style**: `PascalCase`
206: 
207: ```typescript
208: // CORRECT
209: type SearchResult = { score: number; text: string };
210: type MemoryState = 'active' | 'archived' | 'pending';
211: type ScoreCalculator = (input: number) => number;
212: 
213: // INCORRECT
214: type searchResult = { };        // camelCase
215: type search_result = { };       // snake_case
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Const Object Names and Members
219: 
220: **Style**: Prefer `as const` objects over `enum`, with `PascalCase` object names and `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` keys for code maps.
221: 
222: ```typescript
223: // CORRECT
224: export const ErrorCodes = {
225:   NOT_FOUND: 'NOT_FOUND',
226:   TIMEOUT: 'TIMEOUT',
227:   CONNECTION_FAILED: 'CONNECTION_FAILED',
228: } as const;
229: 
230: export type ErrorCodeKey = keyof typeof ErrorCodes;
231: 
232: export const MemoryTier = {
233:   CONSTITUTIONAL: 'constitutional',
234:   WORKING: 'working',
235:   LONG_TERM: 'long_term',
236: } as const;
237: 
238: export type MemoryTierKey = keyof typeof MemoryTier;
239: 
240: // INCORRECT
241: const errorCodes = { NOT_FOUND: 'NOT_FOUND' } as const;  // camelCase object name
242: const ErrorCodes = { notFound: 'NOT_FOUND' } as const;   // camelCase key
243: ```
244: 
245: ### Generic Type Parameters
246: 
247: **Style**: Single uppercase letter or `T`-prefixed descriptive name
248: 
249: ```typescript
250: // CORRECT — simple
251: function identity<T>(value: T): T { return value; }
252: 
253: // CORRECT — descriptive
254: function transform<TInput, TOutput>(input: TInput): TOutput { }
255: interface Repository<TEntity> { }
256: type Mapper<TSource, TTarget> = (source: TSource) => TTarget;
257: 
258: // INCORRECT
259: function identity<type>(value: type): type { }    // lowercase
260: function transform<input, output>(): void { }      // not T-prefixed
261: ```
262: 
263: ### Function Names
264: 
265: **Style**: `camelCase` (unchanged from JavaScript)
266: 
267: ```typescript
268: // CORRECT
269: function calculateDecayScore(age: number): number { }
270: function validateInput(data: unknown): data is string { }
271: async function fetchMemories(query: string): Promise<MemoryRecord[]> { }
272: 
273: // INCORRECT
274: function calculate_decay_score() { }    // snake_case
275: function CalculateDecayScore() { }      // PascalCase
276: ```
277: 
278: ### Constant Names
279: 
280: **Style**: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` (unchanged from JavaScript)
281: 
282: ```typescript
283: // CORRECT
284: const MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 10_000;
285: const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 5_000;
286: const SUPPORTED_MODELS: readonly string[] = ['gpt-4', 'claude-3'] as const;
287: 
288: // INCORRECT
289: const maxQueryLength = 10000;      // camelCase for a constant
290: ```
291: 
292: ### Variable Names
293: 
294: | Scope        | Style        | Example                                     |
295: |--------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------|
296: | Local        | `camelCase`  | `const searchResults: SearchResult[] = []`  |
297: | Module-level | `camelCase`  | `const dbPath: string = '...'`              |
298: | Parameters   | `camelCase`  | `function search(queryText: string)`        |
299: 
300: ### Boolean Names
301: 
302: **Style**: `camelCase` with `is`/`has`/`can`/`should` prefix (unchanged from JavaScript)
303: 
304: ```typescript
305: const isValid: boolean = true;
306: const hasResults: boolean = items.length > 0;
307: const canProceed: boolean = !isBlocked;
308: const shouldRetry: boolean = attempts < MAX_RETRIES;
309: ```
310: 
311: ### File Names
312: 
313: **Style**: `kebab-case` with `.ts` extension (unchanged from JavaScript `.js` convention)
314: 
315: ```
316: memory-search.ts
317: vector-index.ts
318: path-security.ts
319: embedding-provider.ts
320: ```
321: 
322: ### snake_case Exception: Database-Mapped Properties
323: 
324: TypeScript interfaces that mirror SQLite column names MAY use `snake_case` properties. This exception applies **only** to properties that directly map to database columns.
325: 
326: **Rules:**
327: - Include a justification comment on each snake_case property: `// Maps to SQLite column column_name`
328: - For new code, prefer a mapping layer at the DB boundary (map to `camelCase` internally)
329: - Existing interfaces with dual naming (e.g., `MemoryRecord`) are acceptable during migration
330: 
331: ```typescript
332: // ACCEPTABLE — interface mirrors DB schema directly
333: interface MemoryRow {
334:   id: string;
335:   importance_tier: number;   // Maps to SQLite column importance_tier
336:   spec_folder: string;       // Maps to SQLite column spec_folder
337:   created_at: number;        // Maps to SQLite column created_at
338: }
